clue.text: Exercising, thee and me in middle of night?

parts.note: you and me together are us

indicators.note: the centre letter of the five-letter word night is picked out

explanation.surface: Someone working out together with a partner in the small hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of night' gives G, the central letter of NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercising a right or a tool means employing it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Render duet badly but not intimidated

indicators.note: doing something badly scrambles it, so the letters of these two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A pair of singers botch their duet but carry on regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges RENDER DUET.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone undaunted carries on without being put off or scared, a plain synonym.

clue.text: It could be daring, if demeaning

indicators.note: the letters here could be rearranged into something else, signalling a shuffle

explanation.surface: A daring act might also turn out to be beneath one's dignity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges DARING and IF together. INFRA DIG is Latin-derived slang for beneath one's dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: Infra dig describes conduct beneath one's dignity, so it is a synonym for degrading.

clue.text: You may read these at your convenience

definitions.text: You may read these at your convenience

parts.words: You may read these at your convenience
parts.note: a convenience is a British public toilet, whose walls carry scrawled messages; the surface pretends it means at leisure

explanation.surface: Reading material you can get through whenever you have time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at your convenience' seems to mean when it suits you, but a public convenience is a lavatory, where scribbles cover the walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrawled wall writing is famously found in public toilets, called conveniences in Britain.

clue.text: Moneylender's overtures?

parts.note: a lender offers sums up front as loans, and overtures are also approaches made to someone

explanation.surface: A loan shark making opening approaches to a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both loans paid ahead and friendly or romantic approaches; the clue fuses the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Loans paid before they are due and amorous approaches share this one word.

clue.text: Purchases made at a local jumble sale

indicators.note: to jumble letters is to mix them up, so the word sale is rearranged

explanation.surface: Bargains picked up at a village jumble sale.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is a British pub near home; 'jumble sale' looks like one phrase, but 'jumble' rearranges SALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Beers are what one buys at the neighbourhood pub, which Britons call their local.

clue.text: A company that was floated to avoid liquidation ended up here

definitions.text: A company that was floated to avoid liquidation ended up here

parts.words: A company that was floated to avoid liquidation ended up here
parts.note: Noah's ark carried a company of animals afloat to escape the Flood, coming to rest on a mountain in Turkey

explanation.surface: A business floated on the stock market to stave off going bust.
explanation.walkthrough: Business words mislead: 'floated' is literal sailing and 'liquidation' is drowning in the Flood.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis says Noah's vessel came to rest on these mountains after the waters fell.

clue.text: Stays in my group

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: Someone remains among their own crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' reads as a verb but is a noun: stays are the stiffened bodice laced round the torso.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays is the old name for a stiffened, laced foundation garment.

clue.text: Erotic reply to proposal put up, a case for a kiss

indicators.note: the turned reply forms a case holding the kiss
in a down entry, putting something up reads it from bottom to top

parts.note: an accepted marriage proposal is answered yes
X is the conventional written kiss

explanation.surface: A saucy acceptance of a marriage proposal, sealed with a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns YES into SEY, and 'a case for' puts X inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sexually arousing is both erotic and sexy, a close synonym.

clue.text: Furious ace fined for open disobedience

indicators.note: furious suggests wild agitation, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A tennis star, angry at being fined, openly refuses to comply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Furious' rearranges ACE FINED.
explanation.definitionFit: Open resistance or flouting of authority is a synonym for flagrant disobedience.

clue.text: Room for investment?

parts.note: investment here is putting on robes, so the room is where clergy put on vestments

explanation.surface: Scope for putting money into a venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' suggests finance, but it means being invested, clothed in vestments.
explanation.definitionFit: A church room where clergy robe and vessels are kept is the vestry.

clue.text: Exacting examination — the paper's marked in red

definitions.meaning: a decisive trial that proves worth
blue litmus paper turns red in a chemical check for acidity

explanation.surface: A tough exam whose script comes back covered in red ink.
explanation.walkthrough: The red-ink marking is not a teacher's but litmus paper changing colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive trial of quality, and literally the litmus check for acidity.

clue.text: Trade vehicles

definitions.meaning: cars and lorries on the roads

explanation.definitionFit: The word means illicit dealing and also the moving cars on a road.

clue.text: Order me a lilac — or another shrub

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, here the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A garden centre customer asks for a lilac or some other bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' rearranges ME A LILAC.
explanation.definitionFit: This flowering evergreen is a shrub, other than the lilac named in the clue.

clue.text: Totaliser at odds makes one philosophical

indicators.note: being at odds means in disagreement or disarray, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A betting machine showing long odds leaves a punter resigned.
explanation.walkthrough: A totaliser is the tote, a betting machine; 'at odds' rearranges its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek thinker of Stagira is an example of a philosopher.

clue.text: Put in a difficult position and finished full of rage

indicators.note: the first word is filled with the second, which sits inside it

explanation.surface: Someone cornered, ending up seething with fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' splits the word for finished after its third letter and fills it with the rage.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil someone is to put them at risk, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Got back to front

parts.note: suggests something reversed, but means retook first place in a race

explanation.surface: Something put on back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' reads as reversed; it means returned to the front of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor who retakes first place returns to the head of the race.

clue.text: Frank to leave, taking broken clip

indicators.note: the first piece takes the second inside it
something broken is in pieces, so the letters of clip are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Frank walks out carrying a damaged paperclip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the clip, and 'taking' has the word for leave wrap round it. 'Frank' is not a name here but means candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank speech is direct and outspoken, nothing implied, a synonym.

clue.text: Contact one where motor starts with hesitation

definitions.text: Contact one where motor starts with hesitation

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Advice to call a mechanic when a car is reluctant to start.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: motor, then the hesitant 'er'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mechanic is the person you call when a motor misfires on starting.

clue.text: Areas of study lacking in followers

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the small word in is removed

explanation.surface: Academic subjects that fail to attract any adherents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes IN from DISCIPLINES.
explanation.definitionFit: Disciples are adherents of a teacher, like the twelve apostles.

clue.text: It's me dog!

definitions.meaning: the compiler of this puzzle speaking of themselves
a breed of gun dog, such as the red Irish one

explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is the crossword compiler, a convention of self-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: The compiler of a crossword and a breed of gun dog share this word.

clue.text: Packed as a precaution?

definitions.meaning: stowed inside a box or bag
to be ready should something happen

explanation.definitionFit: Placed in a container, and also done against a possible eventuality.

clue.text: Effective narration

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a striking argument and also the act of recounting a tale.

clue.text: He favours dictation above all his subjects

definitions.text: He favours dictation above all his subjects

parts.words: He favours dictation above all his subjects
parts.note: a school-teacher picture, but dictation means dictating orders and subjects are the ruled people

explanation.surface: A teacher whose favourite lesson is dictation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dictation' and 'subjects' suggest a classroom; they mean issuing commands to a ruler's people, and 'above all' means ruling over them.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot rules alone and dictates, set over all the people beneath them.

clue.text: A way through on foot

parts.note: a curved opening forms a passage through a wall, and the raised curve of the sole of the foot bears the same name

explanation.surface: A footpath crossing open country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on foot' looks like walking, but points to part of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved passage under a structure, and the raised curve in the sole.

clue.text: Sends Morse but intercepts call

definitions.meaning: bugs or eavesdrops on a phone line

explanation.definitionFit: Signalling by telegraph key and bugging a phone line share this verb.

clue.text: After the raid it's heard nobody found guilty

definitions.meaning: the siren sounded when an air raid has ended

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain in wartime a siren signalled that bombers had gone.
explanation.definitionFit: The siren signalling safety after bombing, and everyone being exonerated.

clue.text: Yields affected TV shares

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dividends from shares in a television company are hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges TV SHARES.
explanation.definitionFit: Crops gathered in are yields, a synonym in the farming sense.

clue.text: Weary, tried anyway

indicators.note: anyway suggests any old way, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Exhausted, but someone made an effort regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' rearranges TRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being weary means being fatigued and worn out, a plain synonym.
